title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 6-8). For a commutative ring k, Grothendieck builds a simplicial, divided-power version of the de Rham algebra of the standard simplices, using an extra 'homogenising' divided-power variable T. On the previous page, for each n he takes S = k{T}, J = k{T}^+ and t = T. The pd-de Rham complex of the n-simplex is k{X_0,...,X_n}/(ΣX_i - T)_pd ⊗ Λ^•(k^{[n]}/k). In intrinsic form:
- Φ_{k*} = ([n] ↦ k^{[n]}), the k-valued functions on the vertex set [n]. This is a (half-)simplicial k-module.
- Ψ_{k*} = Φ_{k*}/k_diag.
- C^{••}_{DRpd*}(k) = Γ^•_k Φ_{k*} ⊗_k Λ^• Ψ_{k*}. This is a bigraded, strictly anticommutative (odd squares zero) augmented k{T}-algebra with divided powers. Its differential has bidegree (-1,+1): it sends Γ^p⊗Λ^q to Γ^{p-1}⊗Λ^{q+1}, so it preserves the total degree n = p+q.

This page.
(1) The definition is globalised. For a (half-)simplicial set or space X_*, set C^{••}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) := C_{DRpd}(X_*; k{T}, k{T}^+, T) = Hom(X_*, C^{••}_{DRpd*}(k)). This is the analogue of Sullivan's A_PL(X) = Hom_sSet(X, ∇(*,*)), but with divided-power polynomial forms and an extra grading. It is contravariant in X_* and covariant in k.
(2) Key lemma. Φ_{k*} is homotopic to 0 as a half-simplicial k-module. Indeed [n] ↦ Map([n],k) is the 0-coskeleton of k, which is contractible. Degreewise application of a functor preserves simplicial homotopies, so Γ^p(Φ) ⊗ Λ^qΨ ≃ Γ^p(0) ⊗ Λ^qΨ, which is 0 for p ≠ 0. Hence every C^{p,q} with p ≠ 0 is contractible ('acyclic'). The page literally writes 'si p=0'; this must be read as p ≠ 0.
(3) Fix the total degree n. The pd Poincaré lemma on each simplex gives an augmented complex 0 → k_* → C^{n,0}_* → C^{n-1,1}_* → ... → C^{0,n}_*. This is a length-n resolution of the constant object k_* by half-simplicial k-modules. All terms are contractible except the last, Λ^nΨ. Since Ψ ≃ K(k,1), décalage gives Λ^nΨ ≃ K(k,n).
(4) Consequence. The resolution can be viewed as the degree-n truncation of a 'flasque' resolution of k_*. Its complex of sections over X_* therefore computes H^*(X_*,k) truncated at degree n. Result: H^{p,q}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) ≅ H^q(X_*,k) if p ≥ 0, and 0 if p < 0.

Purpose. The next page repackages this as H'^{•,q} ≅ τ_q(H^q(X,k) ⊗_k k{T}), compatibly with products. The aim is a strictly commutative, divided-power, integral (any k) de Rham-type cochain model of a simplicial space. The homogenising variable T replaces the specialisation T = 1, which is not available integrally for divided powers since T^{[n]} ↦ 1/n!. The problem served is a de Rham/Sullivan-type theory with divided powers for the 1976 IHÉS lecture.
errors: The text says C^{p,q} is homotopic to 0 'si p=0'. By the preceding argument (Γ^p(0)=0 for p≠0) and the shape of the resolution (only the last term C^{0,n} is non-acyclic), it should read 'si p≠0'. This is a slip of the pen.

The 'flasque' language is loose. What is used is that contractible half-simplicial k-modules are Hom-acyclic for X_*, together with the identification of the last term Λ^nΨ with K(k,n) via décalage. The latter point is not stated on the page but is needed for the degree-n term to give exactly H^n(X,k).
The case distinction is written as 'q ≤ p [?] i.e. p ≥ 0'. The intended condition is q ≤ n = p+q, i.e. p ≥ 0. The next page also writes H^0 where H^q is meant in its first formula.

ideas.what: Cochain algebra of a simplicial object defined as Hom(X_*, Γ_kΦ ⊗ ΛΨ): a simplicial divided-power polynomial de Rham algebra with homogenising divided-power variable T
ideas.modern_name: Integral / divided-power analogue of Sullivan's A_PL polynomial forms (simplicial pd de Rham algebra)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) and Thom/Whitney for the rational case; Cartan's 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976); integral divided-power forms by Cenkl–Porter (early 1980s) and Karoubi (1990s). Exact attributions unsure.
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA/Pursuing Stacks as far as known; only these 1976 IHÉS lecture notes

ideas.what: Φ_{k*} = Map([n],k) is a contractible simplicial module, so Γ^p(Φ)⊗Λ^qΨ is contractible for p≠0 (degreewise functors preserve homotopy)
ideas.modern_name: Contractibility of the 0-coskeleton; Dold–Puppe homotopy invariance of degreewise functors

ideas.what: For fixed total degree n, the pd de Rham complex of simplices is a length-n resolution of k_* by acyclic objects except the last, giving H^{p,q}_{DRpd}(X,k) ≅ H^q(X,k) for p ≥ 0
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial pd de Rham theorem / Poincaré lemma with truncation; implicit décalage Λ^q(M[1]) ≃ Γ^q(M)[q]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Décalage: Illusie (Complexe cotangent, 1971) and Quillen. de Rham theorem for polynomial forms: Sullivan / Cartan.

missed.claim: A complete integral (arbitrary k) strictly anticommutative, divided-power cochain model of simplicial spaces. It is graded by T-weight and functorial in X and k. For each weight p ≥ 0 its cohomology recovers H^q(X,k) in an explicit, cup-compatible, k{T}-linear way. This predates or parallels the Cenkl–Porter and Karoubi integral forms, and is not credited to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: C^{··}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) =def C_{DRpd}(X_*; k{T}, k{T}^+, T) = Hom(X_*, C^{··}_{DRpd*}(k)) ... H^{p,q}_{DRpd}(X_*,k) ≃ H^q(X_*,k) si p≥0, 0 si p<0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The homogenising pd variable T circumvents the impossibility of integral strictly commutative cochains. Cohomology becomes a k{T}-module τ_q(H^q⊗k{T}) instead of specialising at T=1. This resembles Rees/filtered constructions, e.g. filtered (Hodge-type) refinements in derived de Rham theory. It could be compared with modern results on why integral commutative cochain models must lose information, e.g. Steenrod operations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, correct unpublished construction of an integral divided-power Sullivan-type cochain theory with a homogenising variable, from 1976. The individual ingredients (contractible coskeleton, pd Poincaré lemma, truncation) are standard. The T-homogenised packaging is a notable but not shocking detail, and the page itself is routine bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: Heading: 'Ce structure sera limitée par les' should read 'Ces structures sont héritées par les'.
'à dépendre de façon contravariante' should read 'qui dépendent de façon contravariante'.
'Hom(𝒪_{X_*}, ...)' is more likely 'Hom(X_*, ...)', i.e. sections over X_*.
'𝓛_{k*}' should be 'Φ_{k*}', the object proven homotopic to 0. 'Γ^p_k(𝓛_{k*})' should likewise be Γ^p_k(Φ_{k*}).
'(donc cycliques)' probably reads 'acycliques' (replacing the struck-out 'flasques'). The same applies to 'qui sont cycliques sauf le dernier'.
'si p=0' is as written but should be understood as p≠0.
The end of the exact sequence is 'C^{0,n}_*' (the '[?] ← C^{0,n}_{n+1}' is a misreading of marginal marks). The right margin contains vertical arrows/zeros indicating exactness.
Case condition: 'si q ≤ p+q i.e. p ≥ 0' rather than 'q ≤ p'.
